examDifficulty.heading: Is the Heroku Developer Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers building and operating Heroku apps, including dynos, Procfiles, config vars, add-ons, background work, logging and Heroku Connect.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
68% to pass, which is 41 correct answers out of 60.
Platform details. Dyno types, the Procfile, buildpacks, config vars and add-ons all come up.
Salesforce link. Expect questions on Heroku Connect and calling Salesforce from a Heroku app.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Before the exam, deploy a small app with a database, worker, and Heroku Connect. Use practice tests to identify topics that need another review.

examFormat.heading: Heroku Developer Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Check the current exam guide for the latest format and requirements.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios describe a developer task such as running a migration, handling long work or diagnosing a deploy. Choose the Heroku feature that addresses that task.
bestWayToPass: Know how Procfile process types and release commands work.
Keep configuration and credentials in config vars rather than source code.
Compare read-only and read-write Heroku Connect mappings.
Use logs, metrics and error codes to diagnose app behavior.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers deploying and running Heroku apps, including process types, buildpacks, config vars, add-ons, background jobs, logs and Salesforce integration.

keyConcepts.h2: Heroku Developer AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Buildpacks, Runtime & Procfile
blocks.body: A buildpack turns supported source code into a slug; container deployments use an image instead. A Procfile can define process types such as web, worker and release. The web process must listen on the port provided in the PORT environment variable. A release command runs before the new release’s dynos start, and a failure prevents that release from being activated.

blocks.heading: Config Vars, Add-ons & Environment Management
blocks.body: Config vars hold environment-specific settings and secrets. Updating one restarts the app with the new value. Add-ons provide managed services, such as a database or logging, and may supply their own config vars. Separate staging and production apps in a pipeline so each can have its own settings and services.

blocks.heading: Heroku Connect & Salesforce Integration
blocks.body: Heroku Connect maps Salesforce objects and fields to Heroku Postgres tables. A read-only mapping sends Salesforce changes to Postgres; a read-write mapping can also send changes back. Synchronization can be delayed. An app can use the Salesforce REST API with OAuth when it needs a direct request instead.

blocks.heading: Async Jobs, Workers & Message Queues
blocks.body: Move slow work out of a web request and into a worker dyno. The web process can place a job on a queue for the worker to process. Heroku Scheduler can start one-off dynos for scheduled jobs, and Apache Kafka on Heroku can support event streams. Make jobs safe to retry after interruptions.

blocks.heading: Monitoring, Logging & Performance
blocks.body: Heroku combines router, dyno, and add-on logs through Logplex. Inspect them with `heroku logs --tail` or send them to another service with a log drain. Learn common errors such as H10 and H12, then use metrics to investigate load and memory. You can scale by adding dynos or selecting a larger dyno type.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Heroku Developer Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Translate each developer task into the Heroku process type, add-on or integration feature that handles it.

blocks.heading: Define each process clearly
blocks.body: Use web for HTTP, worker for background work and release for pre-deploy tasks.

blocks.heading: Configure each environment
blocks.body: Use config vars for settings and secrets. Add-ons can provide values such as DATABASE_URL.

blocks.heading: Choose the right Salesforce connection
blocks.body: Heroku Connect syncs mapped records with Postgres; use an API when the app needs a direct operation.

blocks.heading: Design jobs for restarts
blocks.body: A worker job should be safe to retry and should avoid duplicate effects.

blocks.heading: Follow logs to the source
blocks.body: Use app logs and log drains to investigate errors such as memory warnings or request timeouts.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Heroku Developer:

sampleQuestions.question: Which process type runs database migrations before a new Heroku release goes live?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Release process is the best fit because the release process runs after the build and before the new release goes live. If it fails, the release is stopped.
whyWrong: A long-running worker is not the best choice because a worker isn't tied to the release timing.
A README comment is not the best choice because a README doesn't run anything.
The web process is not the best choice because running migrations in the web process can cause errors while dynos start.

sampleQuestions.question: How should the app choose its listening port when Heroku assigns one at runtime?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bind to the PORT variable is the best fit because heroku assigns the port at run time through the PORT variable. An app that listens on a fixed port can't receive traffic.
whyWrong: Increase database capacity is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Bind to the runtime PORT environment variable.
Choose a larger dyno is not the best choice because dyno size doesn't affect which port the app uses.
Use an older buildpack is not the best choice because buildpack version isn't the issue here.

sampleQuestions.question: An app needs its API endpoint and database URL to vary across environments without a code edit. Where should the developer configure them?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Set them as Heroku config vars so the running app receives environment-specific values without embedding secrets or endpoints in source code.
whyWrong: The public app folder is not the best choice because the Procfile lists commands, not secrets.
The Procfile is not the best choice because secrets in code end up in Git history.
Source code is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Heroku config vars.

sampleQuestions.question: How should a developer handle an email job that exceeds the router request window?
options: Queue email work on a worker
sampleQuestions.explanation: Queue email work on a worker is the best fit because the router stops requests after 30 seconds. Long jobs should run on a worker dyno in the background.
whyWrong: Use a larger web dyno is not the best choice because the router timeout can't be raised.
Increase the router timeout is not the best choice because the router cuts the request no matter how long users wait.
Ask users to wait is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Put the email task on a worker queue.

sampleQuestions.question: How can an app query Salesforce Contacts in Postgres without calling Salesforce on every request?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Read-only Connect mapping is the best fit because heroku Connect copies Salesforce records into Postgres, so the app can query them with SQL.
whyWrong: Call Salesforce on every request is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Use a read-only Heroku Connect mapping to Postgres.
Store Contacts in config vars is not the best choice because config vars are for settings, not records.
Upload a weekly CSV is not the best choice because a weekly file goes out of date.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Heroku Connect mapping lets Postgres edits sync back to Salesforce?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Read-write mapping is the best fit because read-write mappings send changes made in Postgres back to Salesforce.
whyWrong: A log drain is not the best choice because followers are read copies of a database.
A database follower is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as A read-write Heroku Connect mapping.
A read-only mapping is not the best choice because read-only mappings only copy data from Salesforce.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a simple way to run a cleanup task every night at 2 a.m.?
options: Keep a web dyno awake until 2 a.m.
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scheduled one-off dyno is the best fit because heroku Scheduler starts a one-off dyno on a schedule to run the task.
whyWrong: Add a release command is not the best choice because manual work is easy to forget.
Run it manually each night is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Use Heroku Scheduler to start a one-off dyno.
Keep a web dyno awake until 2 a.m. is not the best choice because a sleeping web dyno is wasteful and restarts can lose the timer.

sampleQuestions.question: What sends Heroku app logs to an external search and alerting service?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Configure a log drain is the best fit because log drains forward the app's log stream to an outside service.
whyWrong: Create a Review App is not the best choice because review apps are for testing pull requests.
Add a database follower is not the best choice because followers copy database data.
Use a larger dyno is not the best choice because dyno size doesn't affect where logs go.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Heroku R14 warning indicate?
sampleQuestions.explanation: R14 memory limit is the best fit because r14 means memory quota exceeded. The fix is to reduce memory use or move to a larger dyno type.
whyWrong: The app crashed during boot is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as The dyno exceeded its memory quota.
The database is down is not the best choice because database problems show different errors.
A request timed out is not the best choice because a request timeout is H12.

sampleQuestions.question: How does an app learn the connection URL after Heroku Postgres is added?
options: Put the password in source code
Scan the network for a database
sampleQuestions.explanation: DATABASE_URL config var is the best fit because add-ons set config vars automatically. The app reads DATABASE_URL to connect.
whyWrong: Put the password in source code is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Read the DATABASE_URL config var set by the add-on.
Scan the network for a database is not the best choice because apps don't need to search for the database.
Retrieve the URL from email is not the best choice because heroku doesn't send connection details by email.

sampleQuestions.question: The app is working in staging. Which Heroku Pipeline action releases that same build to production?
options: Push source code to production again
Build a new slug with a different buildpack
Copy the files to production over FTP
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use Pipeline promotion to carry the already-built slug forward; production does not need a second build from source.
whyWrong: Push source code to production again is not the best choice because pushing again creates a new build that might differ.
Build a new slug with a different buildpack is not the best choice because a new buildpack produces a different build.
Copy the files to production over FTP is not the best choice because heroku doesn't deploy by FTP.

sampleQuestions.question: How should a background job behave if its dyno restarts before the job finishes?
options: Run every job in a web dyno
sampleQuestions.explanation: Retry-safe job design is the best fit because dynos restart regularly, so jobs should be safe to run again, for example by checking whether the work is already done.
whyWrong: Assume jobs cannot be interrupted is not the best choice because web dynos have the 30-second limit and the same restarts.
Run every job in a web dyno is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Make the job safe to retry without duplicate effects.
Disable dyno restarts is not the best choice because you can't turn off the daily restart.

sampleQuestions.question: Without Heroku Connect, how can the app create a Salesforce Case as soon as a form is submitted?
options: Write to local disk and email it
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce REST API with OAuth is the best fit because the REST API lets the app create records straight away, using an OAuth token for access.
whyWrong: Post the Case to Chatter is not the best choice because a local file is lost on restart and isn't an integration.
Write to local disk and email it is not the best choice because a nightly batch isn't real time.
Wait for the nightly batch is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Call the Salesforce REST API with OAuth.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a quick scaling response when a stateless app’s traffic doubles?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Add web dynos is the best fit because stateless apps scale out easily: more web dynos share the extra traffic.
whyWrong: Turn off logging is not the best choice because removing the database breaks the app.
Remove the database is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Scale out by adding web dynos.
Restart hourly is not the best choice because restarts don't add capacity.

sampleQuestions.question: Which pipeline feature gives reviewers a short-lived app for each pull request?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Review Apps is the best fit because review apps create a short-lived app per pull request and remove it when the pull request closes.
whyWrong: Use Heroku Scheduler is not the best choice because scheduler runs tasks on a timer.
Start one-off dynos is not the best choice because one-off dynos run single commands.
Create another production app is not the best choice because a second production app isn't tied to pull requests.
